subject: 📈 Blue wave surfing

Plus: CVS' dose of separation | Wednesday, November 04, 2026
 
View in browser
 
 
Axios Closer
By Nathan Bomey · Nov 04, 2026

Wednesday ✅. Clouds were lifted last night — both those hanging over the market and the stocks of major cloud computing giants.

Today's newsletter is 806 words, a 3-minute read.

📈 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed up 1.6%, its biggest jump since August.

  • Treasury yields fell and oil prices retreated.

🔥 Today's stock spotlight: Microsoft (+6.7%), Amazon (+6.1%) and Alphabet (+3.2%) rallied on bets that a Democratic-controlled Congress could slow the AI data center construction boom, easing pressure on the tech giants' massive capital spending plans and strained cash flows.
 
 
1 big thing: Blue wave surfing
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

The Democratic Party's blue wave in yesterday's midterm elections washed over Wall Street today, sending stocks sharply higher.

Here are five key takeaways for investors:

🧘 1. The removal of uncertainty is driving market momentum.

  • Traders are happy the midterm elections are over. Now that they know what's next, they're breathing a sigh of relief after a protracted period of uncertainty.
  • "And let's not forget that history shows a big rally post-midterm elections is quite normal and we could be seeing history repeat once again this year," wrote Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.
  • Investors see gridlock as good — and seem to like the fact that the next two years are likely to be defined by it in Washington.
  • "Expect investigations, not legislation," Jefferies analyst Aniket Shah wrote in a research note.

🥶 2. You're probably having a better day in the markets than Elon Musk.

  • OK, so you're not a trillionaire, but your portfolio probably rose today, while Musk's decidedly did not. In fact, he's not a trillionaire anymore either.
  • SpaceX and Tesla shares fell 3.8% and 3.3% today, respectively, despite the broader market rally.

🤖 3. It was a punch to the gut for earthly data center proponents.

  • Voters embraced the equivalent of data center moratoriums in 43 of 44 spots, according to Brad Carson, president of Americans for Responsible Innovation.
  • Tech analyst and AI bull Dan Ives estimated a 10% reduction in data center construction after the backlash.

🪧 4. It was a win for some unions and a loss for others.

  • Union leaders like the UAW's Shawn Fain got what they wanted: a repudiation of what he calls the "billionaire class."
  • But unions representing electricians, plumbers and pipe fitters won't be happy to see the surging opposition to data centers, which are creating trade jobs.

⛽️ 5. Consumers angry about gas prices might get more relief.

  • The U.S. benchmark price of crude oil plunged 8%, falling below $90 per barrel in a potential prelude to lower prices at the pump.

2. A dose of separation
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

CVS is splitting in two, announcing plans today to spin off its retail pharmacy business in 2028.

  • The spin would house the company's 9,000 pharmacies, medical clinic and mail pharmacy businesses.
  • CVS Health would retain its Aetna insurance operation, Caremark pharmacy benefit manager, and specialty pharmacy and health care services businesses.

📉 The impact: Shares closed down 12.5%

🔍 The big picture: CVS is betting the breakup will bring greater operational agility as it rethinks the integrated health care model it spent years building, Axios Pro Deals' Brock E.W. Turner writes.

  • The move also provides some proactive cover from mounting antitrust scrutiny.
  • Regulatory heat on CVS has intensified over the past 18 months, primarily over its pharmacy benefit practices and vertically integrated business model.

3. 🗞️ The readout
 

Photo: Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto via Getty Images
 

🤳 Snap shares slid in extended trading after the Snapchat parent reported lower-than-expected Q3 revenue. (CNBC)

📉 Qualcomm is also falling despite beating Wall Street expectations for the quarter, with a sharp slowdown in smartphone chip sales overshadowing growth in its automotive business. (WSJ)

🍟 McDonald's posted another decline in U.S. same-store sales, but it was slightly better than analysts expected and the stock jumped 6.5%. (Bloomberg)

4. 🕔 After hours: To live and die
By Dan Primack and Nathan Bomey
 

Bryson DeChambeau at a LIV Golf tournament in August. Photo: Justin Casterline/Getty Images
 

Efforts to keep the LIV Golf league alive have collapsed.

  • BC Partners — which had tentatively agreed to invest in a "LIV 2.0" league — is walking away, a source familiar with the matter confirmed today.
  • The league was unable to secure enough support in time to meet the deadlines set in the bankruptcy case.

🏌 Between the lines: At least 30 players ultimately indicated interest in signing on, the source tells us, but economic terms remained a sticking point with some of their representatives.

What's next: People involved in the case expect LIV to pivot to a liquidation.
